summary: A harness.usage reading equal to its slot's last replicated reading stays local instead of replicating again once its five-minute interval passes; per-response readings, which add up, always count

replay.detail: Fewer harness.usage claims are written: a reading whose fields equal the slot's last replicated reading (apart from a native binding the publication added) stays in the host's local observation log, and it supersedes any older pending reading of the slot, so the turn's end has nothing to flush. A reading that differs, and every reading with response semantics (the fold sums those, so two equal responses are two), still replicates on the existing rules. Old claims are untouched.

rules.detail: Checkpoint rules and digests are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: On other nodes a seat's latest usage claim keeps the time of its last change instead of being re-written with the same values every interval. The readers (st usage, the usage budgets, the usage period report and the apps) read the values, which are identical; none reads a usage claim's age. No claim kind, field, wire or CLI contract changes; a mixed-version fleet keeps working, as an older node keeps re-writing and a newer node reads its claims as before.

downtime.detail: No restart beyond the normal upgrade; no migration or backfill.

recovery.detail: No data recovery is needed. Reverting restores the per-interval publication from the next reading; the readings that stayed local remain in each host's local observation log.
